subject: Geo activation latency floor & recovery commitment discussion
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@pioneerbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pioneerbank.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tighter RTO/RPO for west-us primary + carveout proposal

Vivek,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Quick follow up from our infra/ops side — PioneerBank has a regulatory requirement to ensure critical payment flows are recoverable with RTO <= 1 hour and RPO <= 15 minutes for our West-US primary region. Our standard SLOs with vendors are usually 1 hour for critical routes; your public SLA is 4 hours for multi-region activation, which is fine for most of our workloads, but the payments path needs a tighter commitment.

We'd like to understand whether Redwood can:
- Commit to a 1-hour RTO / 15-minute RPO for a scoped subset of endpoints (payments write path + auth) via a contractual addendum.
- Describe activation lead time (how long between declaring failover and full traffic in standby).
- Confirm how many DR tests/year are included and whether tests require customer-scheduled maintenance windows.

We recognize tighter commitments will carry cost/ops implications — we are open to a carveout (reserved capacity + runbook ownership) and want explicit language about degraded latency expectations during failover. Can you share a draft addendum and a rough cost delta?

Regards,
Sam Torres
Head of Infrastructure Ops
PioneerBank

--
Attachment: none
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@pioneerbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO/RPO for west-us primary + carveout proposal

Sam — thanks for the clear summary. We can absolutely scope a commercial/technical addendum that targets the payments path. High-level options we recommend: 

Option A (Gold carveout):
- Contracted warm standby in secondary region with reserved GPU capacity, dedicated traffic routing policy for your payment routes.
- Contractual RTO <= 1 hour for scoped routes (measured from failover trigger).
- RPO <= 15 minutes via cross-region async replication + WAL-forwarding for the payment queue.
- Quarterly DR test windows (one non-prod smoke + one production dry-run) included; additional tests billable.
- Expected latency during recovery: degraded by ~20–40% for short window while caches rebuild; we will include a measurable latency floor in the addendum.

Option B (Silver carveout):
- Shared standby with priority burst capacity; contractual RTO <= 2 hours; RPO <= 30 minutes.

I'll attach a DRAFT addendum and our failover MOP for your review. Cost delta ballpark: Gold ~ +28–40% on hosting/standby capacity vs current committed spend (exact depends on throughput pins).

Next steps: 1) review draft addendum, 2) pick option, 3) schedule a 45-min technical runthrough with Karthik and our SRE team to lock operational controls. Is Tuesday 10/19 10am PT workable?

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivev_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO/RPO for west-us primary + carveout proposal

Looping in a couple of legal/compliance points we should capture in the draft addendum:
- Explicit statement on allowed failure modes (e.g., regional outage vs cascading global outage).
- Testing consent: require at least 7 days notice and a mutually agreed maintenance window for production failover tests.
- Liability cap language for DR activation (we should avoid open-ended credits).
- Auditability: include service-level metrics export (time-to-activate, failover latency histogram) accessible to PioneerBank for 12 months.

Operational suggestion: include an auto-fallback policy where, if the primary failover completes but latency exceeds the advertised floor for >30 minutes, traffic is automatically shifted to a degraded read-only fallback to preserve txn integrity. That reduces RTO risk for payments.

-N
Naomi Feldman
VP, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@pioneerbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pioneerbank.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO/RPO for west-us primary + carveout proposal

Thanks Vivek & Naomi — the options look reasonable. A couple of clarifications before the call: 
1) Activation lead time: when you say RTO is measured from "failover trigger", can you define typical lead time between declaring the trigger (customer or auto) and 50% traffic on the standby? Our runbooks must include that number.
2) DR tests: PioneerBank prefers two full-production failover rehearsals/year, and one emergency failover without notice (to validate on-call readiness). Would Redwood include two production rehearsals in Gold option?
3) Auditing: we require immutable logs for the failover event (who initiated, timeline) retained 24 months. Can you accept that retention?

If those are acceptable we can proceed to a term sheet; also please send the DocuSign link once legal has the addendum.

Sam
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@pioneerbank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO/RPO for west-us primary + carveout proposal

Sam — technical clarifications below (short bullets):
- Activation lead time: for Gold carveout we target 12–18 minutes median to ramp standby to 50% traffic after a manual trigger (typical path: route reconfiguration + canary traffic + KV cache warming). Worst-case 45 minutes under extreme control-plane churn. We'll record the metric and feed it to the audit log.
- RPO mechanics: cross-region async with WAL replication + prioritized log shipping for payment topics. Typical observed RPO < 10 minutes; we guarantee <= 15 minutes in addendum for scoped routes.
- DR tests: Gold includes two production rehearsals/year (we recommend a one-hour smoke window plus a two-hour full-rehearsal). Emergency test without prior notice is allowed once per 12-month period but requires escalation path and agreed runbook steps.
- Retention: event audit trail can be exported as immutable logs to your S3/GCS for 24 months; we will surface a redacted view in Console for 12 months.
- Latency floor: during active failover expect transient P50 increases of 150–350ms on payments write paths depending on cross-region egress; we'll include a SLA clause describing expected degraded tail behavior and an automatic mitigation policy (read-only fallback) if tail exceeds threshold for 30m.

I'll add these bullets into the addendum draft. Happy to demo the runbook during the 10/19 meeting if that still works.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
